[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent Senator [[Elizabeth Warren]] successfully ran for a third term, securing 59.81% of the vote.{{Cite news |date=2024-11-05 |title=Massachusetts U.S. Senate Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-massachusetts-us-senate.html |access-date=2024-11-15 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Warren was challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] attorney [[John Deaton]]. Primary elections took place on September 3, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} This election marked the first time that Warren had lost [[Bristol County, Massachusetts|Bristol County]] while running for the office. Warren underperformed [[Kamala Harris]] by 6 points in the concurrent [[2024 United States presidential election in Massachusetts|presidential election]], making her the second-worst Democratic Senate performer in the 2024 cycle after [[2024 United States Senate election in Maryland|Angela Alsobrooks]] in Maryland. Warren received 84,850 (1.4 percent) votes fewer than Harris. John Deaton ran as an [[Anti-Trump conservative|anti-Trump]] [[Rockefeller Republican|centrist Republican]].{{Cite web |last=Jonas |first=Michael |date=2024-10-16 |title=A feisty Deaton fights to claim middle ground in U.S. Senate race in Mass. • Rhode Island Current |url=https://rhodeislandcurrent.com/2024/10/16/a-feisty-deaton-fights-to-claim-middle-ground-in-u-s-senate-race-in-mass/ |access-date=2025-08-31 |website=Rhode Island Current |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Cristantiello |first=Ross |date=2024-10-15 |title='I'm not loyal to any party': John Deaton pitches himself as moderate alternative to Elizabeth Warren |url=https://www.boston.com/news/politics/2024/10/15/gop-senate-john-deaton-pitches-moderate-alternative-elizabeth-warren/ |access-date=2025-08-31 |website=Boston.com |language=en-US}} {{toclimit|3}} ==Democratic primary== === Candidates === ==== Nominee ==== *[[Elizabeth Warren]], incumbent U.S. senator (2013–present){{Cite web |last1=Kamisar |first1=Ben |last2=Shabad |first2=Rebecca |last3=Vitali |first3=Ali |date=2023-01-20 |title=Democrats Kaine, Warren and Gillibrand are all running for re-election |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/meet-the-press/meetthepressblog/democrats-kaine-warren-gillibrand-are-running-re-election-rcna66714 |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en}} ==== Declined ==== *[[Jake Auchincloss]], U.S. representative for {{ushr|MA|4}} (2021–present){{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/massachusetts-playbook/2023/02/09/rumor-has-it-00081992 |date=February 9, 2023 |title=Rumor has it |author=Kashinsky, Lisa |work=[[Politico]]}} ''([[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Massachusetts#District 4|ran for re-election]])''{{Cite web |last=Kashinsky |first=Lisa |title=N.H.
